referents.why: Third masculine plural suffix on 'secret arts' (their enchantments); the only agreeing possessor that is a sensible doer of enchanting is the magicians (w4), the subject of cl0.
referents.category: possessive suffix on the subject's own instrument

referents.why: Implied subject of a third masculine plural wayyiqtol continuing cl0, whose named subject is the magicians (w4); same agent, the 'also' marks them doing it too.
referents.category: implied subject continuing the previous clause's named subject

links.why: There is no cl2 in this verse; the id is the previous verse's last clause (Exo.8.2#cl2, the land covered). A within-verse 'then' cannot cross a verse boundary, and this verse's cl0 opens a new contrast (the magicians doing the same), not the next event after the frogs covered the land.
links.category: link from a clause outside the verse

links.why: Bringing up frogs is not a later event after 'did thus'; it is what the magicians' doing the same consisted of, so the plain wayyiqtol sequence overstates a time order the sense does not give. Replaced by elaborates.
links.category: detail of an act read as next event

links.why: 'They did thus' (ken) with a named subject (the magicians) who were not commanded: imitation of the deed just done, Aaron stretching out his hand so the frogs came up. Target is the deed begun, Aaron's stretching out (the frogs rising, Exo.8.2#cl1, is its outcome and is also copied).
links.category: others doing the same as a deed just done

links.why: Waw + wayyiqtol 'and they brought up the frogs' says what the 'same thing' was: it is the detail of cl0, not a further act.
links.category: clause giving the detail of 'did the same'

cant_tell.what: Which clause of Exo.8.2 the 'thus' copies: the stretching out (Exo.8.2#cl0) or the frogs coming up (Exo.8.2#cl1)
cant_tell.why: 'Did thus' (ken) does not name the act. The likewise link is written to Exo.8.2#cl0 as the deed begun; the relation holds either way, only the target is unsettled.
